entries.name: Geospatial information technology
entries.definition: The technologies used to collect, store, analyse and display location-based data, such as GIS, GPS and remote sensing.

entries.name: Ghidra
entries.definition: A free, open-source software reverse-engineering suite from the US National Security Agency for disassembling and decompiling programs.

entries.name: GIS mapping
entries.definition: Making and analysing maps with geographic information systems.

entries.name: Glass installation
entries.definition: Cutting, fitting and sealing glass panes, such as windows, doors and mirrors, in frames and openings.

entries.name: Global Mapper
entries.definition: GIS software from Blue Marble Geographics for viewing, editing and analysing geospatial data.

entries.name: GLPI
entries.definition: An open-source web application, developed in France, for managing IT assets and running a help desk.

entries.name: GMP self-inspection
entries.definition: An internal inspection a manufacturer carries out to check its own operations against good manufacturing practice requirements.

entries.name: Go-to-market strategy
entries.definition: Planning how a company will bring a product or service to its target customers, including positioning, pricing and sales channels.

entries.name: Goal setting
entries.definition: Defining clear objectives and the steps and timeline needed to reach them.

entries.name: Gold panning
entries.definition: Separating gold from sand and gravel by swirling the material with water in a shallow pan.

entries.name: Google+
entries.definition: Google's social network, launched in 2011 and shut down for consumers in 2019.

entries.name: Google Ads
entries.definition: Google's online advertising platform for running paid search and display ads, called AdWords before 2018.

entries.name: Google Bard
entries.definition: Google's conversational AI chatbot, launched in 2023 and renamed Gemini in 2024.

entries.name: Google Business Profile
entries.definition: The free Google tool that lets a business manage how it appears in Google Search and Maps, formerly called Google My Business.

entries.name: Google Cloud Platform
entries.definition: Google's suite of cloud computing services, including computing, storage, databases and machine learning.

entries.name: Google Jamboard
entries.definition: Google's digital whiteboard app for collaborative sketching and note-taking, retired by Google at the end of 2024.

entries.name: Google Kubernetes Engine
entries.definition: Google Cloud's managed service for running containerised applications on Kubernetes.

entries.name: Google Optimize
entries.definition: A Google tool for running website A/B tests and personalisation experiments, discontinued in 2023.

entries.name: Google Sheets
entries.definition: Google's web-based spreadsheet application for creating, editing and sharing spreadsheets online.

entries.name: Google Slides
entries.definition: Google's web-based application for creating, editing and sharing presentation slides online.

entries.name: Google Workspace
entries.definition: Google's subscription suite of cloud productivity and collaboration apps such as Gmail, Docs, Drive and Meet, known as G Suite until its 2020 rename.

entries.name: GoPro
entries.definition: A brand of small, rugged action cameras used to record video during activities.

entries.name: GoSystem Tax RS
entries.definition: Thomson Reuters software used by accounting firms to prepare and file tax returns.

entries.name: AI governance
entries.definition: Defining accountable policies and approval conditions for AI use.

entries.name: Government engagement
entries.definition: Building and managing relationships with government officials and agencies to inform policy or win public-sector support.

entries.name: Government finance
entries.definition: The field concerned with how governments raise revenue, budget, spend and manage debt.

entries.name: Graph databases
entries.definition: Representing and querying data through graph structures.

entries.name: Graphical Evaluation and Review Technique
entries.definition: A network-analysis technique for planning projects whose activities have uncertain outcomes and may loop back.

entries.name: Graphics API
entries.definition: Programming interfaces, such as OpenGL, Vulkan and DirectX, that let software send drawing commands to graphics hardware.

entries.name: Graphics Interchange Format
entries.definition: A bitmap image file format, introduced by CompuServe in 1987, that supports 256 colours per frame and simple animation.

entries.name: Graphite
entries.definition: An open-source monitoring tool that stores numeric time-series data and draws graphs from it.

entries.name: Great circle
entries.definition: A circle on a sphere whose centre is the sphere's centre, whose arcs are the shortest routes between two points on the Earth's surface.

entries.name: Greeks (finance)
entries.definition: The measures of how an option's price changes with other factors, such as delta, gamma, theta, vega and rho.

entries.name: Green bond
entries.definition: A bond whose proceeds fund projects with environmental benefits, such as renewable energy.

entries.name: Greeting guests
entries.definition: Welcoming visitors or customers when they arrive in a friendly, professional way.

entries.name: Grieving process
entries.definition: The emotional and psychological process of coming to terms with a significant loss.

entries.name: Groove welding
entries.definition: Joining two pieces of metal by filling a groove cut or formed between them with weld metal.

entries.name: Groundskeeping and yard care
entries.definition: Maintaining outdoor grounds by mowing, trimming, planting, watering and clearing debris.

entries.name: Group decision-making
entries.definition: A process in which a group weighs the options together and reaches a decision.

entries.name: Group work
entries.definition: Working with other people in a group toward a shared task or goal.
